construct.diagnosis_or_process: Primary hypertrophic osteoarthropathy (pachydermoperiostosis) due to impaired prostaglandin E2 catabolism
construct.mechanism: Biallelic HPGD or SLCO2A1 variants can cause primary hypertrophic osteoarthropathy. HPGD loss reduces enzymatic PGE2 degradation, while SLCO2A1 loss impairs cellular prostaglandin uptake needed for clearance. Both mechanisms increase PGE2 exposure and produce digital clubbing, periostosis, arthropathy, and pachydermia.
construct.primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts

source_verification.source: Monoallelic mutations in SLCO2A1 cause autosomal dominant primary hypertrophic osteoarthropathy
source_verification.claim: States that PHO is characterized by clubbing, pachydermia, and periostosis and that HPGD/SLCO2A1 disruption of PGE2 catabolism causes hereditary PHO.

source_verification.source: Mutations in the prostaglandin transporter encoding gene SLCO2A1 cause primary hypertrophic osteoarthropathy and isolated digital clubbing
source_verification.claim: Supports defective prostaglandin transport, reduced metabolic clearance of PGE2, and the PHO phenotype.

second_answer_attack.strongest_alternative: Secondary hypertrophic osteoarthropathy from occult cardiopulmonary disease.
second_answer_attack.resolution: Secondary disease is common, but this patient has a negative cardiopulmonary evaluation, an affected brother, young onset, pachydermia, and elevated PGE2 metabolites. That pattern supports hereditary HPGD/SLCO2A1-mediated impaired PGE2 clearance.
